entities.name: The New Jerusalem
entities.summary: The eternal city of God, descending out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

entities.name: The Twelve Gates
entities.summary: The twelve gates of the New Jerusalem, each a single pearl, inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.

descriptors.statement: The New Jerusalem comes down out of heaven from God.
The city's length, breadth, and height are equal — measured as twelve thousand stadia on each side.
The twelve gates of the city are twelve pearls, each gate being made of a single pearl.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The preciousness, purity, and singular costliness of access to God's eternal city — pearls in the ancient world were among the most valued materials and, unlike gold, are organic and singular rather than fabricated.

descriptors.statement: The names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel are inscribed on the twelve gates.

relations.notes: Twelve gates are part of the city walls (Rev 21:12).
